title: Problem 9.1
content: \textbf{Problem 9.1} Find the moment generating function of the exponential distribution with parameter $\lambda$, and use it to determine the $k$-th moment, for $k\geq 1$.

title: Problem 9.2
content: \textbf{Problem 9.2} Use characteristic function to show that the sum of two independent Poisson random variables is Poisson distributed.

title: Problem 9.3
content: \textbf{Problem 9.3} By using characteristic function, show that the sum of two independent Gamma random variables with distributions $\Gamma(\alpha_1,\beta)$ and $\Gamma(\alpha_2,\beta)$ has distribution $\Gamma(\alpha_1+\alpha_2,\beta)$.

title: Problem 9.4
content: \textbf{Problem 9.4} Show that the characteristic function of $Y=aX+b$ is $\phi_Y(t)=\phi_X(at)e^{ibt}$.

title: Problem 9.5
content:
\textbf{Problem 9.5} Denote the characteristic function of the standard Gaussian distribution by $\psi(t)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Show that the imaginary part of $\psi(t)$ is zero, and
\[
\psi(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\cos(tx)e^{-x^2/2}\,dx.
\]
\item By applying Theorem 9.7, differentiate $\psi(t)$ and derive $\psi'(t)=-t\psi(t)$.
\item Derive $\psi(t)=e^{-t^2/2}$ by solving the differential equation in part (b).
\item Show that the moment of $N(0,1)$ of order $2k$ is $(2k-1)(2k-3)\cdots 3\cdot 1$.
\end{enumerate}

title: Problem 9.6
content: \textbf{Problem 9.6} Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be i.i.d. Cauchy random variables. Show that $(X_1+\cdots+X_n)/n$ is Cauchy with the same distribution as $X_1$.

title: Problem 9.7
Problem 9.8
content: \textbf{Problem 9.8} Prove that $\phi_X(2\pi)=1$ if and only if $P(X\in\mathbb{Z})=1$.

title: Problem 9.9
content: \textbf{Problem 9.9} Let $\phi_X(t)$ denote the characteristic function of a random variable $X$. Given any $n$ distinct real numbers $t_1<t_2<\cdots<t_n$ in ascending order, define an $n\times n$ matrix $M$ by letting the $(i,j)$-entry be $m_{ij}=\phi_X(t_j-t_i)$. Prove that $M$ is Hermitian and positive semi-definite. That is, show that $M^H=M$ and $v^H Mv\geq 0$ for all complex vectors $v\in\mathbb{C}^n$. The superscript $H$ means conjugate transpose.

title: Problem 9.10
content: \textbf{Problem 9.10} It is known that the characteristic function of a $\chi^2$ distribution with $k$ degrees of freedom is $(1-2it)^{-k/2}$. Find the mean and variance.

title: Problem 9.11
content: \textbf{Problem 9.11} Prove that if $\phi(t)$ is the characteristic function of a random variable, the squared magnitude $\lvert\phi(t)\rvert^2$ is also a characteristic function.
